culture.title: Submarine Tour at OMSI
culture.description: A hands-on science museum on the river whose best exhibit is moored outside — the USS Blueback, the last diesel-electric sub the Navy commissioned.
culture.bonus: Take the sub tour, not just the museum ticket.

culture.title: Pittock Mansion and the View Below It
culture.description: A 1914 French Renaissance house on a hill a thousand feet above the city, with a lawn that frames downtown and Mount Hood in one shot.
culture.bonus: Walk up from Lower Macleay instead of driving to the lot.

culture.title: Repertory Night at the Hollywood Theatre
culture.description: A 1926 movie palace run as a nonprofit, showing 70mm restorations, cult programming and its own Kung Fu Theater series.
culture.bonus: Check what's screening in 70mm and build the night around it.

culture.title: Grand Floral Parade at the Rose Festival
culture.description: The city's oldest civic tradition — a century-old parade of all-floral floats through downtown, with a visiting fleet and a waterfront carnival around it.
culture.bonus: Watch from the Hollywood district stretch rather than the downtown crush.

culture.title: Stand-Up at Helium Comedy Club
culture.description: A proper comedy club on Southeast Hawthorne that pulls touring headliners and runs a genuinely good local open-mic scene midweek.
culture.bonus: Go on a midweek night and watch the locals work new material.

culture.title: Portland Art Museum
culture.description: The oldest art museum in the Northwest, strongest in Native American art, Northwest modernism and a serious print collection.
culture.bonus: Find the Center for Contemporary Native Art before you leave.

culture.title: Matchday with the Timbers Army
culture.description: One of the loudest supporter sections in North American sport — three thousand people in the north end singing, drumming and holding tifo for ninety minutes straight.
culture.bonus: Get a seat in or beside the north end, not across from it.

culture.title: Oregon Historical Society Museum
culture.description: The state's story told properly, including the parts about Oregon's founding exclusion laws that most visitors never hear.
culture.bonus: Spend real time in the Experience Oregon exhibit rather than skimming it.

chill.title: Soak and Steam at Knot Springs
chill.description: A soaking club above the Burnside Bridge with hot and cold pools, a steam room and a wall of windows over the river and the east side.
chill.bonus: Do three full hot-cold cycles before you get in the sauna.

chill.title: Tea House Afternoon at Lan Su Garden
chill.description: A full Ming-dynasty scholar's garden built by artisans from Suzhou, occupying one city block of Old Town, with a two-storey tea house above the lake.
chill.bonus: Order a pot at the Tower of Cosmic Reflections and stay for a full steeping.

chill.title: Pour-Over and a Slow Hour at Deadstock
chill.description: A sneakerhead coffee shop in Old Town where the drinks are named after basketball and nobody minds if you sit for an hour.
chill.bonus: Ask what's on the shelf behind the counter.

chill.title: Bloom Season at Crystal Springs
chill.description: Seven acres of rhododendrons, a spring-fed lake and a heron colony tucked behind Reed College — at peak bloom it is genuinely absurd.
chill.bonus: Cross every bridge in the garden before you leave.

chill.title: Dig the Crates at Music Millennium
chill.description: The oldest record store in the Pacific Northwest, still stacked floor to ceiling, still hosting in-store sets on a stage by the door.
chill.bonus: Buy something purely because of the cover.

chill.title: Wander the Hoyt Arboretum Ridgeline
chill.description: Twelve miles of trails through a living collection of trees from around the world, laid out along the ridge above Washington Park.
chill.bonus: Walk the Redwood Trail and stand under the coast redwoods.

chill.title: Wander the Portland Japanese Garden
chill.description: Follow the winding paths through five garden styles, past koi ponds and a teahouse, in what's regarded as the most authentic Japanese garden outside Japan.
chill.bonus: Sit by the Heavenly Falls for five full minutes before moving on.

chill.title: Soak at Common Ground Wellness Cooperative
chill.description: Book a private outdoor hot tub session at this member-run co-op tucked into a Southeast Portland backyard.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in the changing room for the whole session.

chill.title: Browse the Stacks at Powell's City of Books
chill.description: Get lost for an afternoon in a full city block of new and used books across nine color-coded rooms.
chill.bonus: Buy one book from a section you never browse.

chill.title: Picnic and People-Watch at Laurelhurst Park
chill.description: Spread a blanket under the old-growth trees at one of Portland's original Olmsted-designed parks and do nothing in particular.
chill.bonus: Bring a book you've been meaning to start and read one full chapter.

adventure.title: Kayak Out to Ross Island
adventure.description: Rent from Alder Creek and paddle the Willamette around Ross Island Lagoon, where herons and osprey nest a mile from downtown.
adventure.bonus: Paddle the full lagoon loop and count the osprey nests.

adventure.title: Trail of Ten Falls at Silver Falls
adventure.description: Loop the canyon at Silver Falls State Park and walk behind the curtain of South Falls on a trail that strings together ten waterfalls in one hike.
adventure.bonus: Stand behind the water at South Falls and get the photo looking out.

adventure.title: Ride the Sandy Ridge Trail System
adventure.description: Purpose-built flow trail an hour east of the city, where you shuttle up the gravel road and drop into bermed singletrack the whole way down.
adventure.bonus: Link Hide and Seek into Follow the Leader without putting a foot down.

adventure.title: Wildflower Climb up Dog Mountain
adventure.description: A relentless 2,800-foot climb on the Washington side of the Gorge that pays out in May with an entire summit meadow of balsamroot.
adventure.bonus: Take the Augspurger route down for the quieter descent.

adventure.title: Soak at Bagby Hot Springs
adventure.description: Hike a mile and a half of old-growth forest to hand-hewn cedar tubs fed by piped spring water deep in the Mount Hood National Forest.
adventure.bonus: Take a private tub rather than the communal deck.

adventure.title: Switchback up Beacon Rock
adventure.description: Climb a hand-built catwalk of fifty-odd switchbacks bolted to the face of an 848-foot volcanic plug for one of the best views in the Gorge.
adventure.bonus: Count the switchbacks on the way up and see if you agree with the sign.

adventure.title: Wildwood Trail Through Forest Park
adventure.description: Drop into one of the longest urban forest trails in the country and walk fir-shaded switchbacks until the city noise disappears entirely.
adventure.bonus: Find the Stone House ruins off the Lower Macleay approach.

adventure.title: Learn to Windsurf in Hood River
adventure.description: Take a lesson in the Columbia River Gorge, where the river current runs one way and the gorge wind screams the other — the wind-sport capital of the country.
adventure.bonus: Stay for a beer on the Hood River waterfront and watch the pros in the swell.

adventure.title: Loop the Volcano at Mt. Tabor Park
adventure.description: Walk the ridgeline of an honest-to-god extinct volcano crater without leaving the city limits.
adventure.bonus: Find the reservoir with the best skyline view and take a photo there.

adventure.title: Day Trip to Haystack Rock in Cannon Beach
adventure.description: Drive out to the Oregon Coast and stand at the base of a 235-foot sea stack while tide pools reveal starfish at your feet.
adventure.bonus: Time it around low tide and find a purple ochre sea star.

adventure.title: Chase Falls Along the Historic Columbia River Highway
adventure.description: Pull off at Multnomah Falls, then keep driving the old highway for three more waterfalls most tourists never find.
adventure.bonus: Skip the first waterfall's crowd and go straight to your third stop.

adventure.title: Hike Angel's Rest for a Gorge-Wide View
adventure.description: Switchback up 1,600 feet through burned and regrown forest to a bare rock outcrop with the whole Columbia River Gorge laid out below.
adventure.bonus: Pack a thermos and drink your coffee at the summit, not before.

adventure.title: Boulder at The Circuit Bouldering Gym
adventure.description: Get a day pass and work the bouldering walls at this Central Eastside gym, one of Portland's most popular climbing spots.
adventure.bonus: Try a route at least one grade harder than your usual.

adventure.title: Ski or Ride a Full Day at Mt. Hood Meadows
adventure.description: Drive up to the mountain and spend the day on runs with views clear across the Cascades, an hour and a half from downtown.
adventure.bonus: Take one run you'd normally skip because it looks too hard.

adventure.title: Bike the Eastbank Esplanade Loop
adventure.description: Ride the floating path along the Willamette River and loop back over one of Portland's iconic bridges for a skyline view from the water.
adventure.bonus: Stop on the bridge deck and count how many bridges you can see from there.

social.title: Rooftop Drinks at Departure
social.description: Fifteen floors up on the roof of the Nines, a retro-futurist deck with two terraces and the best west-side sunset view downtown offers.
social.bonus: Get on the west terrace before sunset, not after.

social.title: Work Your Way Down North Mississippi
social.description: Six walkable blocks of bars, patios and food carts — start at one end, have one drink per stop, and see how far you get.
social.bonus: Finish at a food cart pod rather than a restaurant.

social.title: Cider Flight at Portland Cider House
social.description: Oregon apples turned into everything from bone-dry to marionberry, poured by the flight in a Hawthorne pub that takes cider as seriously as beer.
social.bonus: Try the driest one on the board first and recalibrate from there.

social.title: Dance on the Floating Floor at the Crystal Ballroom
social.description: A 1914 ballroom with a mechanical floor mounted on ball bearings — when the room jumps, the whole floor moves with it.
social.bonus: Stand in the middle of the floor during the loudest song and feel it bounce.

social.title: Sour Flight at Cascade Brewing Barrel House
social.description: The house that Northwest sour ales built — order a flight of barrel-aged fruit sours and work from the least to the most aggressive.
social.bonus: Ask what's just come off the barrel that week.

social.title: Cocktails at Multnomah Whiskey Library
social.description: A wood-panelled room with rolling ladders and 1,500-plus bottles, where a bar captain wheels a cart to your table and builds the drink in front of you.
social.bonus: Let the captain pick something you've never heard of.

social.title: Portland Night Market in the Central Eastside
social.description: A warehouse full of local makers, food vendors and drinks that takes over an industrial block for a handful of weekends each year.
social.bonus: Buy one thing from the first vendor that stops you.

social.title: Last Round at the Sandy Hut
social.description: A red-lit Portland dive with decades of history, cheap pours and booths that have absorbed a great many stories.
social.bonus: Play something on the jukebox that clears the room.

social.title: Game Night at Guardian Games
social.description: Grab a table at this board game store and café and challenge a stranger — or a friend — to something you've never played before.
social.bonus: Ask the staff to recommend a game neither of you has heard of.

social.title: Pinball and Pixels at Ground Kontrol Classic Arcade
social.description: Feed quarters into a wall of vintage arcade cabinets and pinball machines at this 21-and-up bar arcade downtown.
social.bonus: Find the oldest machine in the building and set a house high score.

social.title: Private Room Karaoke at Voicebox
social.description: Rent a private room with a friend group and work through the entire songbook without an audience of strangers.
social.bonus: Everyone has to sing one song solo, no duets allowed.

social.title: Dance Until Close at Holocene
social.description: Hit the dance floor at this Southeast Portland club known for its rotating DJ lineup and unpretentious crowd.
social.bonus: Compliment a stranger's dance moves before the night's over.

foodie.title: Pie and a Beer at Apizza Scholls
foodie.description: Thin, blistered, fiercely traditional pizza from a kitchen that caps its dough per night and closes when it runs out.
foodie.bonus: Get there when the doors open — they stop when the dough is gone.

foodie.title: Duck Stack and Onion Soup at Canard
foodie.description: Gabriel Rucker's all-day bar next door to Le Pigeon, where the menu runs from a duck-fat pancake stack to French onion soup you dip like a sandwich.
foodie.bonus: Order the steam burger and the duck stack and share both.

foodie.title: Breakfast Line at Pine State Biscuits
foodie.description: Buttermilk biscuits under fried chicken, bacon and sausage gravy — the Reggie Deluxe is the order and the line is part of the deal.
foodie.bonus: Eat it on the curb like everyone else rather than waiting for a table.

foodie.title: Saturday Morning at the PSU Farmers Market
foodie.description: The biggest farmers market in the city fills the South Park Blocks every Saturday with Oregon produce, cheese, hazelnuts and a dozen breakfast stalls.
foodie.bonus: Build an entire breakfast from three different stands.

foodie.title: Khao Man Gai at Nong's
foodie.description: One dish, done perfectly: poached chicken over rice cooked in the broth, with a ginger-soy-chili sauce that made this cart a Portland institution.
foodie.bonus: Order the chicken soup on the side. It comes from the same pot.

foodie.title: Zakuski and Horseradish Vodka at Kachka
foodie.description: Russian and Georgian small plates built for drinking — herring under a fur coat, pelmeni, and an infused vodka list you work through as a table.
foodie.bonus: Order the full Zakuski spread and let the kitchen choose.

foodie.title: Thai Tasting Menu at Langbaan
foodie.description: A reservation-only room hidden behind a bookcase, serving a rotating regional Thai tasting menu unlike anything else in the city.
foodie.bonus: Book the counter so you can watch the pass.

foodie.title: Korean Dinner at Han Oak
foodie.description: Peter Cho cooks Korean-American family food out of a converted courtyard home in the Central Eastside — dumplings, noodles and whole-animal plates.
foodie.bonus: Sit in the courtyard if the weather allows.

foodie.title: Food Cart Crawl at Hawthorne Asylum
foodie.description: Work through a lineup of a dozen-plus carts in one pod and build a meal from three different countries' cuisines.
foodie.bonus: Split every dish with whoever you're with — no ordering your own plate.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Le Pigeon
foodie.description: Sit at the open kitchen counter and let one of Portland's most decorated restaurants send out course after course of French-inspired plates.
foodie.bonus: Ask the chef what they'd order if it were their night off.

foodie.title: Doughnut Run at Voodoo Doughnut
foodie.description: Order something genuinely strange — bacon maple bar, cereal-crusted, whatever's in the case — from Portland's most famous doughnut counter.
foodie.bonus: Order the weirdest flavor on the board, no substitutions.

foodie.title: Ice Cream Flight at Salt & Straw
foodie.description: Taste your way through five rotating scoops, from the classics to seasonally weird ones like pear-and-blue-cheese.
foodie.bonus: Let the person next to you pick your weirdest flavor.

8ball.title: Ride the MAX to the End of a Line You've Never Taken
8ball.description: Buy a day pass, pick whichever MAX line you know least, and ride it to the last stop. Whatever is within four blocks of that platform is the plan.
8ball.bonus: No looking up the destination before you get there.

8ball.title: Take the Tram Up and Walk All the Way Back Down
8ball.description: Ride the aerial tram from the South Waterfront up to Marquam Hill, then find your own route back down through the hills on foot.
8ball.bonus: Take a street you've never walked instead of the marked trail.
